List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday,  the May 11, 2006/Vaisakha 21, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and
Information Technology; External Affairs; Information and Broadcasting;
Overseas Indian Affairs; Panchayati Raj; Parliamentary Affairs;

Visit of the former Thai Foreign
Minister to North-Eastern States
*381. SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government’s attention has
been drawn to the recent visit of the former
Thai Foreign Minister to North-Eastern
States accompanied by a group of
academicians from South East Asia with a
view to understand India’s Look East
Policy  whereunder they had an
interaction with the students of Guwahati
University;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
delegation broached the conceptualization
of Ganga-Mekong Subarna Bhumi idea;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether Government propose to
conceptualize the said idea by formulating
any policy in this regard; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Unoccupied Government
accommodation in Delhi
*382. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of Government
accommodations that remained unoccupied
during the last five years in Delhi;
(b) what was the revenue loss to
Government on account of unoccupied
houses, year-wise;
(c) whether Government propose to
consider proposal of deducting Licence Fee
and HRA only from the Government
employee, who occupies the flat and not
from his/her spouse, who is also a
Government employee in order to have
higher occupancy of Government
accommodation and higher revenue to
Government; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?

120
Authorized agents under Emigration
Act, 1983
*383. SHRI AMAR SINGH: Will the
Minister of OVERSEAS INDIAN
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the number of authorized agents
under Emigration Act, 1983 in Hyderabad
who have been recruiting labourers for
foreign countries and how many labourers
have been sent by each of them to foreign
countries during the last two years;
(b) whether Government are aware that
a few agents whose licenses have expired
since long have been sending labourers to
foreign countries with connivance of
Protector of Emigrants, Hyderabad;
(c) if so, the names of such recruiting
agents and the number of workers sent by
them after the expiry of their licenses; and
(d) what action Government have taken
against them and the Protector of Emigrants,
Hyderabad?
Defining poverty line
*384. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of URBAN
EMPLOYMENT AND POVERTY
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are
serious flaws in the methodology adopted
by Government in defining poverty line as
it makes very little provision for other
essentials of life like drinking water, shelter
and sanitation;
(b) whether it is a fact that the rate of
decline of poverty since 1973 has been at
dismal 0.81 per cent per annum and the
number of poor stood at about 25 crore in
2004; and
(c) if so, the steps Government propose
to take to include parameters like drinking
water, shelter etc., in the definition of
poverty?
Relaxing of norms under Delhi
Master Plan
*385. SHRI BASHISTHA NARAIN
SINGH: Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether in view of suggestions
received on Delhi Master Plan 2021 and
ground reality, Government have re-looked
at Floor Area Ratio, dwelling units and
height norms for plotted residential
housing;
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor;
(c) the progress made/decision taken on
suggestions to increase number of dwelling
units to four in plots of sizes 100-250 sq.
metres keeping in view the existing reality
of lakhs of such units all over Delhi; and
(d) the status of report of Task Force
on rehabilitation colonies which was to look
into these issues?
Interest rate on Seamens Provident
Fund
*386. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
 Will the Minister of SHIPPING,
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Seamens Provident
Fund attracts less interest than the
Employees Provident Fund;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government are considering
the issue of making the rate of interest
uniform;
(d) if so, the details of the measures
being taken; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?

121
Mapping of resources in remote and
inaccessible areas of NER
†*387. SHRI JANESHWAR
MISHRA: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the mapping
of resources in the remote and inaccessible
areas of North-East is being done through
satellites by using remote sensing technique;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, whether Government are
considering to make any special provision
to carry out this task; and
(d) if so, the details thereof, State-wise?
Rohini Residential Scheme of DDA
*388. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Rohini
Residential Scheme, 1981 of DDA
envisaged allotment of 90 sq. mt. plots in
MIG category;
(b) if so, the number of 90 sq. mt. plots
allotted and date of  last allotment;
(c) whether it is also a fact that later on,
an option was given to applicants to opt
for 60 sq. mt. plots for early allotments;
(d) if so, whether any 90 sq.mt. plots
were allotted after calling the options; and
(e) if not, the purpose of calling options
if all plots of only 60 sq. mt. were to be
allotted and the reasons for disturbing
priority list by making out of turn
allotment?
Development of Maritime Industry
*389. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of SHIPPING,
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) the steps proposed by Government
to ensure that various hurdles are not put
by the Mercantile Marine Department in
discharging their duties;
(b) what specific objection Government
have if Indian boat and ship owners get
their surveys done abroad at recognized
shipyards;
(c) to what extent is the MMD harming
the entrepreneurs; and
(d) the steps proposed to bring about
reforms in this sector?
Borrowing of Central Police Organi-
zation’s officers by CBI
*390. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Central
Bureau of Investigation is unable to
investigate various cases including housing
scam due to shortage of manpower;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the CBI
is planning to borrow officers from the
Central Police Organization to meet its
demand; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Nyaya Panchayat Bill
*391. SHRI SHANT ARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Nyaya Panchayat Bill
which Government propose to introduce
in Parliament is ready;
(b) if so, the essential features of the
Bill; and
(c) the response, if any, of the State
Governments to the proposed Bill?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

122
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Opening of Indo-Pak border in
Ferozepur
*392. SHRI VARINDER SINGH
BAJWA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal to
open Indo-Pak border at Hussainiwala in
Ferozepur district of Punjab;
(b) if so, whether any negotiations are
going on with Pakistan; and
(c) the status of the talks?
New spectrum policy
*393. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the reasons for announcing new
spectrum allocation policy for GSM and
CDMA telecom operators without waiting
for the recommendations of Group of
Ministers (GoM);
(b) whether PMO and GoM have
endorsed the policy announced by DoT;
(c) if not, whether DoT would retract
or keep on hold the announcement until
the GoM formulates a comprehensive
spectrum policy; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Land for Kerala Industrial Park
*394. SHRI N.K. PREMA-
CHANDRAN: Will the Minister of
URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether any proposal of the Kerala
Government seeking transfer of unutilized
land from Government of India Press at
Koratty in Kerala to KINFRA for setting
up of Industrial Park is pending for
sanction; and
(b) the present stage of the proposal
for land transfer and if the decision for
transfer of land has been arrived at, the
details thereof?
Funds allocated for the development
of National Highways
†*395. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of
SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that for the
development and maintenance of National
Highways in the financial year 2005-06
approximately twenty seven hundred crore
rupees were allocated to all the States; and
(b) if so, the State-wise details of the
amount allocated, released and spent and
the number of States that have sent
utilization certificates to Central
Government.
Handing over of Kachatheevu Island
to Sri Lanka
*396. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Kachatheevu
Island was given to Sri Lanka under an
agreement;
(b) if so, the details of the agreement;
(c) whether Sri Lanka has been abiding
by the agreement, so far; and
(d) the consequences that would follow
in the event of Sri Lanka violating the
agreement?

123
Funds allocated for opening of post
offices in Andhra Pradesh
*397. SHRI C. RAMA-
CHANDRAIAH: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of new post offices
proposed during the current financial year,
State-wise;
(b) the number of post offices and sub-
post offices already opened so far,
State-wise; and
(c) the details of the funds allocated
for this purpose and the amount spent till
date, State-wise, particularly in Andhra
Pradesh?
National Scheme of Liberation and
Rehabilitation of Scavengers
*398. SHRI LALIT SURI: Will the
Minister of URBAN EMPLOYMENT
AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the amount sanctioned upto 31st
March, 2005 to Uttar Pradesh under
National Scheme of Liberation and
Rehabilitation of Scavengers and their
dependants;
(b) the amount utilized upto 31st
March, 2005 by the State Government for
the training and rehabilitation of the
scavengers and their dependants under the
scheme; and
(c) the number of persons who have
been benefited till 31st March, 2005 under
the scheme in the State with specific figures
for the cities of Lucknow, Kanpur and
Allahabad?
Agreement with Bangladesh
*399. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
SHRI LALIT SURI:
 Will the PRIME MINISTER  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether India and Bangladesh both
have agreed to work closely on security,
trade and river water sharing;
(b) if so, what were the main agreements
reached during the recent talks;
(c) the steps being taken to implement
these agreements; and
(d) whether there has been any
improvement between the two countries
on these issues?
Mine expansion programme of NLC
*400. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Prime Minister, while
inaugurating the Golden Jubilee
Celebrations of Neyveli Lignite
Corporation, announced the Corporation’s
Rs. 4,200 crore mine expansion programme;
and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,

Long term energy security
2711. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BAL
APTE: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have recently
formulated a nuclear power programme to
provide long-term energy security to the
country based on the indigenous nuclear
fuel resources;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the stage at which it stands at
present?
Reserves of uranium in Orissa
†2712.  SHRI Y ASHWANT SINHA:
   SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL:
 Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a huge reserve
of uranium has been discovered  in the
Vemlagarh and Sayamba region of the
Sundargarh district of Orissa;
(b) whether it is also  a fact that a team
of the scientists is making efforts to discover
and calculate the availability of the huge
potential  of  uranium reserve; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Criteria for setting up of Nuclear
Power Plants
2713. SHRI VARINDER SINGH
BAJWA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) the criteria laid down for setting up
Nuclear Power Plants;
(b) the States which have requested the
Central Government  to set up such  plants;
and
(c) the action taken  by Government in
each case?

Availability of thorium
2714. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the percentage of thorium used  in
the nuclear reactors in the country out of
the total  nuclear fuel;
(b) the potential availability of thorium
in the country as nuclear fuel; and
(c) the steps taken to increase use of
thorium to avoid dependence on uranium
import?
Preservation of fruits in Jammu and
Kashmir
2715. SHRI T.S. BAJWA: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Bhabha Atomic
Research Centre has developed a technique
of long lasting preservation of fruits;
(b) if so, whether this technique has
been tried in Jammu and Kashmir; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Production of coal
†2716. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Coal
India Limited(CIL)  and its subsidaries have
carried out more production  of coal in the
year 2005-06 than 2004-05;
(b) if so, the quantity of coal produced
by the both during the above period,
separately; and
(c) the turnover  of the coal producing
units  during  the above period?
Private investment in coal sector
†2717. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether  it is a fact that Government
have decided to allow the private sector for
making capital investment in the coal  sector;
(b) if so, the facts in this regard; and
(c) by when this decision is likely to be
implemented?
Sliding work force in coal sector
2718. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the work
force in coal industry is sliding  gradually;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) what has been the per employee
production in coal industry during the last
five years, year-wise?
Profits and dividends from CIL and
other subsidiaries
†2719. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA: Will the Minister of
COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Coal
India Limited (CIL) and other subsidiary
coal producing units are expected to earn a
profit of Rs. 7000 crores during 2005-06;

(b) if not, the estimate in this regard;
(c) whether the said amount of dividend
is higher than last year’s dividend; and
(d) if so, the extent thereof?
Commonwealt Games
2720. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI: Will the Minister of YOUTH
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to
state:
(a) the major steps taken for the hosting
of Commonwealth Games in New Delhi;
(b) whether we have made efforts or
proposed to take measures to train our
sportspersons to perform extraordinary in
Commonwealth Games in North Delhi;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Handing over of captive coal mines to
private companies
†2721. SHRI RAMADHAR
KASHYAP: Will the Minister of COAL
be pleased to state:
(a) the purpose of handing over captive
coal mines to the private companies;
(b) the date of handing over the captive
coal mine to the WCL based Central
Collieries company, year-wise, the quantity
of coal extracted/produced from the said
mine alongwith the market value of the
same;
(c) whether the Central Collieries
company has sold this coal in open market;
(d) whether the said company has not
generated even a single unit of electricity
from this coal; and
(e) if not, the action being taken by
Government against the company for selling

Captive coal mines under SECL
†2722. SHRI RAMADHAR
KASHYAP: Will the Minister of COAL
be pleased to state:
(a) the number of captive coal mines
allotted under S.E.C.L. indicating the names
of the companies alongwith the name of
mines so allotted;
(b) whether these companies also sell
their coal to other companies besides their
internal use;
(c) if so, the details of the companies to
whom this coal was sold during the last
five years alongwith the quantum of coal
sold and its value and rate in each case; and
(d) the detail of Government’s policy
in this regard?
Utilization of USO funds
2723. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that more than
half of the money (Rs. 7,000 crore out of
Rs. 10,753) that telecom consumers pay
for creation of rural telephony
infrastructure is lying unused in
Government coffers;
(b) whether the finance Ministry is to
be blamed for this under-utilisation of funds
as it controls the Universal Service
Obligation (USO) fund collected; and
(c) if so, the steps Government propose
to take to make maximum utilization of
USO fund?

Shortfall of coal from indigenous
sources
2724. SHRI S. ANBALAGAN: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that shortfall of
coal from the indigenous sources has been
increasing every year;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the steps
proposed to be taken thereon;
(c) whether there is any initiative to use
judiciously this non-renewable indigenous
source of coal in the country and to find
environment friendly alternative source of
energy in place of coal; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Coal accumulation in Jharkhand
†2725. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that heavy stock
of coal has accumulated at the pit head of
three coal companies namely, CCL, BCCL
and ECL situated in Jharkhand;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps being taken by
Government in this regard?
Regulatory Commissions for Coal and
Telecommunications
†2726. SHRI LAXMINARAYAN
SHARMA: Will the Minister of COAL be
pleased to state:
(a) whether any regulatory Commission
is likely to be constituted for coal also on
the lines of the similar commission
constituted for  Power and Telecommuni-
cation, so that, interests of the consumers
are protected; and
(b) if so, by when?
Setting up of kiosks under Saksham
project
2727.  SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
 SHRI B.J.PANDA:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Microsoft Corporation
has announced their rural initiative
"Saksham" under which the company
would partner with NGOs to roll out
50,000 kiosks over the next three years;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of such kiosks which are
proposed to be set up in Orissa with the
Central assistance?
Disbursal of USO Fund for rural
telephony
2728. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have expressed dissatisfaction at slow
progress of the disbursal of Universal
Service Obligation Fund for rural
telephony;
(b) whether it is a fact that the scheme
is taking too long to reach the take off stage
and the slow progress of disbursal is
harming Government's plan to ensure 200
million mobile subscribers by the year
2007; and
(c) if so, the efforts Government
propose to make to ensure the scheme is
implemented expeditiously?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Cost of money orders
2729. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION  TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any plans
to reduce the existing cost of money orders;
(b) if so, the steps proposed to make
the system of money orders speedy,
efficient and economical;
(c) the steps taken by Government
during the last six months to make money
orders commercially viable and attractive
to the public;
(d) whether any tie-ups with banks has
been mooted by the post offices; and
(e) if so, the details of the steps
proposed in this regard?
Participation of foreign mobile
companies
†2730. SHRI  UDAY PRATAP SINGH:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn towards increasing
participation of domestic mobile
companies with the foreign mobile
companies;
(b) if so, the names of those companies
which have a participation with the foreign
companies;
(c) whether Government's attention has
been drawn towards direct or indirect danger
to the country's security due to increasing
participation of foreign companies; and
(d) if so, the preventive steps being
taken in this regard?
Shortage of software and hardware
engineers
2731. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a shortage of
software and hardware engineers in the
country;
(b) if so, whether Government have
assessed the actual requirement of software
and hardware engineers;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) the number of engineers coming out
of professional colleges in each State as on
date; and
(e) the steps taken/proposed to be taken
to ensure all of them are absorbed within
the country?
Withdrawal of notices by VSNL
2732. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the VSNL
had issued notices on 2nd March, 2006 to
some MNCs and foreign carriers for the
termination of remote access connectivity
and DoT had to ask VSNL to withdraw the
same;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) whether all the notices have been
withdrawn by VSNL; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Sales Tax on telecom services
2733. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Hon.
Supreme Court has held that the States can't
impose sales tax on telecom services;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) its impact on the proposed budgeted
revenue for the financial year 2006-07?
Printing of BSNL telephone
directories
†2734. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION  TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
responsibility to print and distribute the
telephone directories rests with the Bharat
Sanchar Nigam Limited and these
directories should be printed and
distributed to the subscribers every year;
(b) whether it is a fact that directories
have not been distributed in several
divisions for the last 5-6 years;
(c) whether it is also a fact that Bharat
Sanchar Nigam Limited, Jaipur district has
not got the directories printed so far; and
(d) whether any action would be taken
against the District Officers of the
Corporation for this negligence?
Software Technology Park in Bihar
†2735. SHRI SHATRUGHAN
SINHA: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION  TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
of Bihar has handed over three acres of
land and Rupees one crore to the Centre
under an agreement to construct a Software
Technology Park in the State;
(b) if so, the progress made so far in
this scheme; and
(c) whether the State Government has
recently approached the Centre in this
regard?
Telephone connectivity in villages of
H.P.
2736. SHRI SURESH BHARDWAJ:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a)  the telecom density in the rural areas
in the country with particular reference to
the hilly areas like Himachal Pradesh,
Uttaranchal and Jammu and Kashmir; and
(b) whether there is any proposal to
connect more villages and provide telecom
facilities to every village in Himachal
Pradesh?
Disinvestment of BSNL
